surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the reduction of tantalum(V) using trimethylaluminum (TMA) as a reducing agent. The TMA pulse introduces surface species that react with tantalum chloride (TaCl5) and ammonia (NH3). The reaction mechanism includes the formation of surface hydroxyl groups and the subsequent reduction of tantalum, leading to the formation of tantalum nitride (TaN) and the release of byproducts such as methane (CH4) and hydrogen chloride (HCl).
evidence: The text describes the use of trimethylaluminum (TMA) as a reducing agent in the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Ta~Al!N~C! thin films. It mentions that the TMA pulse introduces surface species that react with tantalum chloride (TaCl5) and ammonia (NH3). The reduction of tantalum(V) is facilitated by TMA, leading to the formation of tantalum nitride (TaN) and the release of byproducts such as methane (CH4) and hydrogen chloride (HCl). The surface reactions are self-limiting and involve the formation of surface hydroxyl groups and the subsequent reduction of tantalum. The text also notes that the decomposition of TMA during the deposition process contaminates the films with aluminum and carbon, which are incorporated into the film structure.
